summary: Leela Aditi Wood specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Michigan in 2005 under Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Leo Frobenius worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He held positions at the Frobenius Institute (1920–1938), Goethe University Frankfurt (1932–1938), the Museum der Weltkulturen (1935–1938), and the Berliner Gesellschaft für Anthropologie, Ethnologie und Urgeschichte.

Leo M. Pruden was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (1964–1966) under Akira Hirakawa and Taitetsu Unno. He taught at Brown University (1970–1971), Nyingma Institute (1971, attested 1991), and the University of Oriental Studies (attested 1988–1991).

Leo Meyer was a linguist who studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and Berlin under Jacob Grimm, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at Göttingen (professor 1862–1865, chair 1898) and the University of Tartu (1865–1899).

Leo Strauss was a philosopher who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, Marburg, and Columbia. His academic posts included Cambridge (~1934–1937), Columbia (~1937–1938), Hamilton College (~1938), The New School (~1938–1949), University of Chicago (~1949–1969), Claremont McKenna, and St. John's College (~1969–1973).
Leon Hurvitz worked in Buddhist studies and sinology. He held professorial posts at the University of Washington (~1955–1971) and the University of British Columbia (~1971–1988).

Linguist Leonard Bloomfield earned degrees from Harvard and Chicago and studied at Leipzig and Göttingen. He held posts at Chicago, Cincinnati, Illinois (1910–1921), Ohio State (1921–1927), Chicago again (1927–1940), and Yale as Sterling Professor of Linguistics (1940–1949).
Leonard Blussé is a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied at Leiden University (~1965–1970) and later held a post there from 1998 to 2011.

Leonard C. D. C. Priestley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and F. E. L. Priestley. He held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1991).

Leonard Swidler was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who earned degrees from Marquette, Wisconsin-Madison, and Tübingen. He held posts at Duquesne University (1960–1966) and served as Professor of Catholic Thought and Interreligious Dialogue at Temple University (1966–2022).
Leonard Woolley was an archaeologist and historian. He was educated at St John's School, Leatherhead (~1893–1899) and New College (~1899–1903).
Leonard Zwilling is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison until 1976 and was a student of Ngawang Wangyal.

Leonard van der Kuijp is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD and DPhil at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served at the University of Washington (~1987–1995) and became a professor at Harvard University in 1995.

Leopold Pospisil studied at Charles University, Willamette, Oregon, and Yale. He became a professor at Yale University in 1956 and served as curator of anthropology at the Peabody Museum of Natural History (~1956–1993).

Leopold von Schroeder was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Tartu, Leipzig, Jena, and Tübingen. He held academic posts at the University of Tartu (1882, 1890), University of Innsbruck (1896), and University of Vienna (1899).

Leslie S. Kawamura worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Saskatchewan (~1970–1975) under Herbert V. Günther and served as a professor at the University of Calgary (~1976–2004).

Levi McLaughlin focuses on religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Princeton, he held posts at Kokugakuin, Wofford College, National University of Singapore, University of Iowa, and became associate professor at North Carolina State University in 2012.

Lewin Bentham Bowring worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Chief Commissioner for the Government of Mysore (~1862–1870) and was later affiliated with the University of Mysore.

Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at SOAS under Ulrich Pagel. He has held research and teaching posts at the British Museum, Free University of Berlin, University of Munich, and University of Bonn.

Lewis Hodous was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Case Western, Hartford, and Halle-Wittenberg. He served as president and head of Foochow Union Theological School (1902–1917) and professor at Hartford International University for Religion and Peace (1917–1945).
